items.title: Telangana student goes missing in US; minister seeks MEA, Boston Police intervention
points: A 23-year-old student from Telangana has gone missing in Boston in United States, prompting state minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy to seek urgent intervention from the ministry of external affairs, the Boston Police and relevant agencies.
The student, identified as Sreeja Reddy Koya, is pursuing her higher education at the University of Massachusetts Boston.
The Boston Police issued a missing person alert for her, which said she had been missing since November 2..
In their alert issued on November 5, the Boston Police requested public assistance in efforts to locate the 23-year-old, while also providing details of her whereabouts before she went missing.
The cops said that Sreeja was last seen leaving her residence in Dorchester's Edison Green at around 9.45 pm on November 2.
The cops said they were actively working to locate her and urged anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911 or contact District C-11 (Dorchester) Detectives at (617) 343-4335.

items.title: IL JIN Electronics files draft papers for ₹2,500-crore IPO
points: IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd files preliminary papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise ₹2,500 crore through an IPO.
IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, an arm of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed preliminary papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise ₹2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6.

The company plans to use the proceeds to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts.

items.title: Former Tech Mahindra business head shot dead by neighbour over parking dispute in Faridabad
points: Former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour following a dispute over parking in Faridabad’s Sector 21C on Friday night.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, was settled in Singapore and was presently working as the senior vice president of FPT Software Company Limited, which is headquartered in Vietnam.

According to the police, the suspect, identified as Mohan Sharma, allegedly opened fire on Dhankhar with his licensed pistol, firing around 15 rounds, nine of which hit the victim, killing him on the spot.

On complaint of the victim’s son, Shaurya Dhankhar, an FIR under section 103(1) (murder) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act was registered at Surajkund police station on Saturday, police said.

On Friday night, the Dhankhar and Sharma again got into an argument over parking a vehicle, following which Sharma allegedly called Dhankhar out of his home and shot him multiple times with his licensed pistol.

A High-Level Steering Committee, headed by the Chief Minister, will be constituted to monitor the implementation of the scheme.

items.title: Volkswagen Tiguan R-Line Discontinued In India
points: For a considerable amount of time, Volkswagen Tiguan R-Line stood tall as the brand’s flagship offering in the country.
This 5-seater premium mid-size SUV was launched in India in April 2025 and it was imported into the country as a CBU (Completely Built Unit).
Even though the company has not made any public announcements, Volkswagen Tiguan R-Line has now been discontinued from India and is de-listed from the official website.
Tiguan R-Line’s last recorded price tag was Rs 47.11 lakh (Ex-sh) and the company has now de-listed it from their official website, hinting at a possible discontinuation from the Indian market.
In terms of prices, Tayron R-Line is priced at Rs 47.74 lakh (Ex-sh), which is around the same price tag as Tiguan-R Line.

items.title: Delhi Schools Go Hybrid Up To Class 5 As AQI Hits 382 Ahead Of Diwali
points: New Delhi: Parents of children up to Class 5 in Delhi can now choose to keep them home for online lessons as the capital's pollution inches closer to the "severe" category just ahead of Diwali.
The Delhi government has ordered schools to conduct classes up to Class 5 in hybrid mode with immediate effect, allowing students to attend lessons either online or in person.

The directive covers government, government-aided and recognised private schools under the Directorate of Education, as well as those run by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) and Delhi Cantonment Board.

items.title: Death Count In Assam Oil India Fire Rises To 2, 5 Injured Remain Critical
points: The death count in the massive fire that broke out at an Oil India Limited (OIL) installation in Assam's Dibrugarh district has risen to two, with five injured persons continuing to remain in critical condition.
Tapas Jyoti Gogoi, who had sustained severe burn injuries in the incident, died during treatment at a private nursing home in Dibrugarh on Wednesday.
His death comes a day after Raju Dutta died following the fire and explosion at the facility.
Meanwhile, Oil India Limited has constituted an internal inquiry committee to investigate the incident.
According to a statement issued by the PSU, a fire was reported on Friday at the Indirect Bath Heater (IDBH) of the Intermediate Tank Farm (ITF) at Tengakhat.
The incident occurred in an indirect bath heater area that had been taken up for maintenance and had remained isolated since November 4.
The fire broke out around 9:05 am during maintenance work at the Intermediate Tank Farm following an explosion.

items.title: As tracks pierce isolated red region, Chhattisgarh’s Abujhmad finds a route to progress

Construction for the 95km Dallirajhara–Rowghatt railway line, which has 26 operational stations between Raipur and Rowghat, began in 2015.

items.title: Maharashtra to lease reservoir land for fodder cultivation in 304 drought-hit talukas
points: The Maharashtra government has decided to lease exposed cultivable land in reservoirs and tanks across 304 drought-declared talukas to farmers and livestock owners for growing short-duration fodder crops, Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod…
The decision is aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock in areas affected by rainfall deficiency during the 2026 kharif season.
The Soil and Water Conservation Department issued technical guidelines on November 5, outlining the conditions for cultivation, land allotment and water use.
According to Mr. Rathod, farmers will be permitted to cultivate fodder crops such as maize, sorghum, pearl millet, nutrifeed, berseem and oats on eligible land under the department’s jurisdiction.

To protect reservoir infrastructure, cultivation will be prohibited within 50 metres of the reservoir-side toe of an earthen dam, and within 30 metres of spillways, their approach areas and structures such as outlets, intake wells, jackwells, gauge poles…
Under the allotment process, officials from the Revenue, Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Soil and Water Conservation departments will conduct joint surveys to identify eligible land.

items.title: Delhi Building Collapse Deaths Rise To 3 As Body Recovered After 47 Hours
points: The death count in the building collapse in Old Delhi's Hauz Qazi area has risen to three after rescuers recovered another body from the debris, even as rescue operations continued at the site on Saturday.

According to officials, the body of Pankaj Sharma (40), son of Hazari Sharma and a resident of Bihar's Khagaria district, was recovered during the ongoing search and rescue operation at the collapse site in Gali Sitara near Chawri Bazar Metro station.
With the latest recovery, a total of five people have been rescued or recovered from the debris so far, including three people who died and two injured persons.
Both injured persons have received medical treatment and are now stable.

items.title: Toyota Innova Hycross & Hyryder Hybrids Set New Records For Elevation Gains

items.title: Delivery Agent Injured, Glass Shattered In Explosion At Ghaziabad Police Post
points: A blast at the Vasundhara Police Outpost in Ghaziabad on Friday night triggered an investigation by multiple agencies.
The explosion, which occurred around 9 pm, damaged the police facility, shattering two glass panes and cracking one of its walls.
At the time of the incident, a Sub-Inspector posted at the police outpost and a delivery executive, who had arrived to deliver an order, were present at the spot.
The delivery executive sustained injuries after being hit by shattered glass and was taken for medical treatment.
"The glass panes of two windows at the outpost were shattered, and a crack appeared.
He is now completely healthy," Rijul Kumar, DCP Ghaziabad, said.
Shortly after the incident, a banned group, 'Tehreek-ul Mujahideen Hindustan ', claimed responsibility for the blast.
Teams from the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL), Bomb Disposal Squad, and Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) reached the spot and collected evidence.

items.title: Oil Companies Reject Karnataka's '31% Ethanol In Petrol' Claim, Question Sampling Procedure
points: Public sector OMCs have rejected Karnataka's claim that petrol sold at some retail outlets in the state contained up to 31 per cent ethanol, saying the findings were not based on testing carried out under the prescribed procedures.

The Karnataka government alleged that major oil marketing companies were supplying petrol with ethanol content above the prescribed 20 per cent limit, with tests recording levels as high as 31.2 per cent, and sought action against the companies.

Addressing a press conference, Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad said the allegations were based on tests on petrol samples collected from Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara,…
"The OMCs would like to clarify that the claims, as reported, are not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures," the statement said.
The companies said E20 petrol supplied by them across the country, including Karnataka, conformed to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline.
